newsitem.title: USA: U.S. 1996 budget deficit shrinks to lowest in 15 years.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 1996 budget deficit shrinks to lowest in 15 years.

text.p: The White House on Monday announced that the fiscal 1996 U.S. budget deficit had shrunk to $107.3 billion, its lowest level in 15 years, from 1995's $163.9 billion.

President Bill Clinton was expected to trumpet the figures in a St. Louis campaign speech later, using them to argue that he has managed the economy well and more than delivered on his 1992 campaign promise to cut the deficit in half.
The White House said in a document released in St. Louis that the deficit for fiscal 1996, which ended September 30, represented 1.4 percent of gross domestic product, the lowest share since 1974.
It added that that overall the budget deficit had fallen by 63 percent during the four years of Clinton's presidency.

Franklin Raines, the director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), which compiles the figure, said that the drop reflected stronger-than-expected growth, which raised tax revenues, as well as efforts to hold down government spending.
"About half is from the increase in economic growth and about half is from holding down spending," he told reporters in St. Louis, Clinton's third stop on a three-day, seven-state campaign trip.

In Washington, congressional Republicans sought to argue that Clinton did not deserve credit for the decline in the deficit, while in St. Louis, Raines argued that the Republican contribution had been limited.
"The spending reductions since the Republican majority has been in place have been relatively modest compared to the overall total," Raines said.
"Although we have been able work with them in the last year on the mutually acceptable budget ... if we had been able to do (that) earlier these numbers could have been much better," he said.
Raines also said he expected the fiscal year 1997 budget deficit to be lower than the $144 billion that OMB estimated in March, largely because growth was likely to be stronger than then expected.
